facts.statement: Aleosteus is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Early Devonian period.
facts.quote: Aleosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm fish of the Early Devonian period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Aleosteus include almost complete juvenile and adult specimens characterized by a short, broad skull that is concave at the back.
facts.quote: Almost complete fossils belong to juvenile and adult specimens and show a short and broad skull, posteriorly concave.

facts.statement: The type species Aleosteus eganensis was described in 2000 from fossils found in the Late Emsian strata of the Sevy Dolomite Formation in the Egan Range of east-central Nevada, USA.
facts.quote: The type species Aleosteus eganensis was described in 2000, and was found in the Late Emsian strate of the Sevy Dolomite Formation, in the Egan Range of east-central Nevada, USA.

facts.statement: The species name eganensis is derived from the Egan Mountain Range where the type locality is located.
facts.quote: The species name eganensis is based on the type locality in the Egan Mountain Range in Nevada.

facts.statement: Aleosteus is considered a basal member of the order Arthrodira and is closely related to the genus Simblaspis.
